Legacy_Thresholds: Continuous (0 to 1). Higher = more codes exceeding frequency limits.

Legacy_Purpose: Standardizes total billed distance against the full provider population. Identifies providers whose total transportation footprint is unusually large.
Legacy_Clinical_Context: Unlike mileage_zscore_class which looks at per-procedure quantities, this measures total distance across all trips. A provider with normal per-trip distance but extremely high total distance is running many trips.
Legacy_Peer_Group: All providers (entire population mean and standard deviation for total_distance)
Legacy_Note: df['z_score_distance'] = (df['total_distance'] - df['total_distance'].mean()) / df['total_distance'].std()

Replacement: Paid units compared with all providers
Description: How far paid units sit above or below the units paid to other providers for the same procedure (the comparison group is not confirmed).
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when far above peers, especially if units per patient are also high; consistent with frequency abuse or excessive visits.
Benign_Explanations: Large caseloads, providers paid in small time units, and specialties with high-volume codes.
Narrative_Caveat: Totals grow with caseload and code type; if units per patient is also listed, describe them together.
Value_Template: The provider's paid units ranked at the {peer_pct} percentile among {category} providers.
Records_To_Review: Paid units by code, member and month; progress notes, trip sheets or delivery tickets for the top-unit members; prior authorization file.
Policy_Lever: Unit edit: cap paid units per member per period for high-volume codes; review providers far above peers.
Open_Question: Derivation is (QUANTITY_PAID - mean)/std: confirm whether this is per claim line or on provider totals, and whether peers are all providers or the same category.

Original_Description: How unusual this provider's total billed quantity is compared to all providers
Legacy_Replacement: How unusual this provider's total billed quantity is compared to all providers
Legacy_Purpose: Standardizes total billed quantity against the full provider population. Helps distinguish high-volume providers from typical ones.
Legacy_Clinical_Context: A high z-score here combined with normal per-procedure z-scores suggests the provider simply handles more patients. A high z-score here WITH high per-procedure z-scores suggests systematic overbilling.
Legacy_Peer_Group: All providers (entire population mean and standard deviation for QUANTITY_PAID)
Legacy_Note: df['z_score_quantity_paid'] = (df['QUANTITY_PAID'] - df['QUANTITY_PAID'].mean()) / df['QUANTITY_PAID'].std()

Description: How far above or below other transport providers the provider's paid mileage units are, compared code by code; large positive values mean far more.

Narrative_Caveat: Continuous version of the mileage tier; narrate only one of the two. If miles per trip is also listed, describe them together.
Value_Template: The provider's paid mileage ranked at the {peer_pct} percentile among providers paid for the same mileage code.
Records_To_Review: Trip sheets, driver logs and dispatch records; GPS or odometer data for top-mileage trips; pickup and drop-off addresses vs mapped distance.
Policy_Lever: Edit: compare paid mileage units with mapped route miles; pend claims far above peers for the same code.

Confirm the name mapping. PER_MILE_PROC_CDS includes T2005, a per-trip stretcher van code; if this feature uses that list, trips are counted as miles.

Legacy_Replacement: Continuous z-score measuring how far this provider's mileage procedure billing deviates from peers

Replacement: Average patient-level checks flagging each patient
Description: Average number of the 5 separate patient-level checks that flagged each of the provider's patients (0 means none, 5 means all).
Suspicious_Pattern: Context only: a high average means the provider's patients often stand out in the separate patient-level screening.
Benign_Explanations: Patients with complex, high-cost conditions stand out on several checks; small caseloads swing the average.
Narrative_Caveat: Introduce as added context ('In addition, ...'); from a separate patient-level screening, not a reason this provider was flagged.
Value_Template: In addition, the provider's patients were flagged by an average of {value} of 5 patient-level checks (peer median {peer_median}; provider at the {peer_pct} percentile).
Records_To_Review: Patient-level screening results for the flagged members; their paid claims across all providers; clinical record review for a sample.
Policy_Lever: Audit: sample records of the provider's patients flagged by several patient-level checks.
Open_Question: Confirm the 5 patient-level checks and the cutoff each uses to flag a patient.
Change_Note: Removed 'model' and 'anomalous'; framed as separate patient-level screening context, not a driver.
Original_Description: Average number of models (out of 5) that flagged each patient across this provider's panel
Legacy_Replacement: Average number of models (out of 5) that flagged each patient across this provider's panel
Legacy_Purpose: Measures model consensus on patient anomalies. A provider whose flagged patients average 4/5 model agreement has stronger signals than one averaging 2/5.
Legacy_Clinical_Context: Higher consensus means the patient anomalies are robust across different detection methods (IF, AE, OCSVM, KMeans, LOF). Low consensus may reflect borderline cases or model-specific artifacts.
Legacy_Peer_Group: All patients of this provider
Legacy_Thresholds: Continuous (0 to 5). Higher = stronger consensus across models.
Legacy_Note: Behavioral metric from patient perspective combine step.

Replacement: Most patient-level checks flagging one patient
Description: Highest number of the 5 separate patient-level checks that flagged any single patient of this provider.
Suspicious_Pattern: Context only: a high value shows at least one patient stood out on many checks; it says nothing about the rest of the caseload.
Benign_Explanations: One medically complex or high-cost patient can reach the top value.
Narrative_Caveat: Introduce as added context ('In addition, ...'); from a separate patient-level screening, not a reason this provider was flagged.
Value_Template: In addition, the most-flagged patient of this provider was flagged by {value} of 5 patient-level checks (peer median {peer_median}; provider at the {peer_pct} percentile).
Records_To_Review: Patient-level screening results for the flagged members; their paid claims across all providers; clinical record review for a sample.
Policy_Lever: Audit: review records of the single most-flagged patient.
Change_Note: Removed 'model' and 'anomalous'; framed as context about one patient only.
Original_Description: Highest number of models that flagged any single patient in this provider's panel
Legacy_Replacement: Highest number of models that flagged any single patient in this provider's panel
Legacy_Purpose: Identifies the worst single patient. A provider with at least one 5/5 consensus patient has an extremely anomalous individual in their panel.
Legacy_Clinical_Context: Useful for distinguishing: many mildly anomalous patients (high pct_flagged, low max) vs. few extreme patients (low pct_flagged, high max). The former suggests systematic issues; the latter suggests specific phantom or captive patients.
Legacy_Peer_Group: All patients of this provider
Legacy_Thresholds: Integer (0 to 5). 5 = at least one patient flagged by all models.
Legacy_Note: Behavioral metric from patient perspective combine step.

Description: Among the provider's patients flagged in the separate patient-level screening, the average number of different providers each one was paid to see.
Suspicious_Pattern: Context only: many providers per flagged patient can mean patients spread across providers; very few can mean patients kept with one.
Benign_Explanations: Complex patients see many specialists; rural patients may have only one provider.
Narrative_Caveat: Introduce as added context ('In addition, ...'); from patient-level screening, not why the provider was flagged. No good or bad direction.
Value_Template: In addition, patients flagged in patient-level screening saw an average of {value} different paid providers (peer median {peer_median}; provider at the {peer_pct} percentile).
Records_To_Review: Patient-level screening results for the flagged members; their paid claims across all providers; clinical record review for a sample.
Policy_Lever: Audit: compare the flagged patients' other providers for shared referral or ownership ties.
Open_Question: Confirm whether 'providers' counts all providers or only those of the same type.
Change_Note: Removed 'anomalous'; kept both directions as context only; added rollup caveat.
Original_Description: Average number of distinct providers seen by this provider's flagged (anomalous) patients
Legacy_Replacement: Average number of distinct providers seen by this provider's flagged (anomalous) patients
Legacy_Purpose: Measures whether flagged patients are concentrated at one provider or spread across many. If flagged patients see many providers, the anomaly may be patient-driven. If they see few, it may be provider-driven.
Legacy_Clinical_Context: A flagged patient seeing 8 different DME providers is a patient-level anomaly (possible beneficiary fraud). A flagged patient seeing only this one provider is a provider-level anomaly (possible captive panel). The distinction matters for investigation strategy.
Legacy_Peer_Group: All flagged patients of this provider
Legacy_Thresholds: Continuous. Low values (1-2) suggest provider-driven anomaly. High values suggest patient-driven anomaly.
Legacy_Note: Behavioral metric from patient perspective combine step.

Replacement: Share of payments from flagged patients
Description: Share of the provider's total payments that came from patients flagged in the separate patient-level screening.
Suspicious_Pattern: Context only: a high share means much of the provider's money comes from patients who stood out in patient-level checks.
Benign_Explanations: Flagged patients are often high-need, high-cost patients; a few such patients can drive most of a small provider's payments.

Records_To_Review: Patient-level screening results for the flagged members; their paid claims across all providers; clinical record review for a sample.

Original_Description: Proportion of this provider's total payments attributable to flagged (anomalous) patients
Derivation (col G): sum(PMT_AMT for flagged patients) / sum(PMT_AMT for all patients).
Legacy_Replacement: Proportion of this provider's total payments attributable to flagged (anomalous) patients
Legacy_Purpose: Measures financial exposure from anomalous patients. A provider where 80% of revenue comes from flagged patients has high-risk revenue concentration.

Original_Description: Percentage of this provider's patient panel flagged as anomalous by patient-level models
Derivation (col G): Computed in combine_provider_perspective_scores.py from patient-level model flags rolled up to provider. Explicitly NOT a model input - a behavioral metric carried alongside scores.

Legacy_Purpose: Measures what fraction of the provider's patients exhibit anomalous patterns. A provider with 40% of patients flagged has a systemic issue, not isolated bad actors.
